summary: Audited all direct store.writeWorkPackage() and store.writeRootIndex() calls outside LedgerStore class methods. Confirmed WP-001 and WP-002 successfully eliminated all three bypass paths in work-package.ts (createWorkPackage, propagateDependencyUnblock, propagateDependencyReblock).

Verified no redundant manual last_updated = now() stamps remain on WP detail objects in former bypass paths. The root index last_updated stamps (lines 396, 1010, 1102 in work-package.ts) are not redundant — they stamp the root index object, not the WP detail.

Added @internal JSDoc comments to writeWorkPackage and writeRootIndex in ledger-store.ts explicitly marking them as internal methods callable only from LedgerStore sync methods, with the project-lifecycle.ts self-healing exception documented.

Remaining direct writeRootIndex calls in observations.ts, workflow-handoff.ts, project-lifecycle.ts (init and completeSynthesis), and auto-archive.ts are all legitimate root-only writes (no concurrent WP write) — they are not bypass paths and are correctly outside scope. The writeWorkPackage calls in project-reset.ts are in an explicit withLock admin utility, also correctly outside scope.
All 1432 tests pass with zero failures (exceeds the 1418+ target).

comments.note: The @internal JSDoc tag on writeWorkPackage and writeRootIndex documents the intended access boundary clearly, but TypeScript has no enforcement mechanism for @internal. If stricter access control becomes desirable in the future, these methods could be renamed with an underscore prefix (_writeWorkPackage, _writeRootIndex) or moved to a private inner class. For now the documentation comment is sufficient and non-breaking.

project-reset.ts (src/utils/project-reset.ts lines 401, 415, 511) calls writeWorkPackage directly within its own withLock scope — a pattern that predates the sync method consolidation. This is a valid admin utility pattern but represents a divergence from the choke-point architecture. A future cleanup could migrate it to batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync to also gain auto-stamping and validation guarantees there.

observations.ts (src/tools/observations.ts line 174) calls writeRootIndex for project-comment-only updates (no WP changes). Since there is no corresponding WP write, using the sync methods is not applicable here. This is correct as-is, but a future writeRootIndexWithSync convenience wrapper (root-only, with lock) could unify the root-write pattern across all callers.

summary: Independent audit confirmed all four acceptance criteria are met. Zero direct store.writeWorkPackage() calls exist in src/tools/ — the three former bypass paths (createWorkPackage, propagateDependencyUnblock, propagateDependencyReblock) now correctly route through createWorkPackageWithSync and batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync. The only remaining store.writeWorkPackage() calls are in src/utils/project-reset.ts within an explicit withLock admin pattern, which is a documented valid exception. Both writeWorkPackage and writeRootIndex carry @internal JSDoc in ledger-store.ts clearly stating they must only be called from LedgerStore sync methods, with the project-lifecycle.ts self-healing exception documented. No redundant WP-detail last_updated = now() stamps remain in the former bypass paths — root index last_updated stamps at lines 396, 1010, 1102 in work-package.ts are on rootIndex objects (not WP details), which is correct. The project-lifecycle.ts getProjectStatus() self-healing pattern (line 434) is intact and uses its own explicit lock. Full test suite: 1432 tests passed, 44 test files, zero failures.

comments.note: The @internal JSDoc boundary is documentation-only — TypeScript has no enforcement for this tag. If the constraint becomes critical to enforce, a future option is renaming both methods with underscore prefix (_writeWorkPackage, _writeRootIndex) as a convention signal, or extracting them into a private inner class. Current documentation is sufficient for now.

Edge case verified: the root-index last_updated stamps inside propagateDependencyUnblock (line 1010) and propagateDependencyReblock (line 1102) operate on the rootIndex object that is returned as { root: rootIndex } from the batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync callback — these are not bypass writes and are correct.

No test specifically exercises the @internal boundary (i.e., no test asserts that tool functions cannot call writeWorkPackage directly). This is acceptable for a JSDoc-only constraint, but a future architectural test (e.g., a static analysis or import graph check) could encode the boundary as a failing test if the pattern ever drifts.

summary: WP-003 is a documentation-only change (JSDoc additions to writeWorkPackage and writeRootIndex in ledger-store.ts). Full structural review completed: zero bypass paths remain in src/tools/, all three former bypass paths (createWorkPackage, propagateDependencyUnblock, propagateDependencyReblock) confirmed routed through createWorkPackageWithSync and batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync. @internal JSDoc on both methods is accurate, well-scoped, and clearly identifies the project-lifecycle.ts self-healing exception. project-reset.ts withLock admin pattern is a valid exception that predates the sync consolidation. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: The @internal JSDoc on writeRootIndex documents the project-lifecycle.ts self-healing exception clearly (line 179-180 of ledger-store.ts). One minor gap: writeRootIndex does not document the other known legitimate direct callers (project-reset.ts admin lock, auto-archive.ts, observations.ts, workflow-handoff.ts). The current comment says tool functions 'must NOT call this directly' but does not enumerate the accepted exceptions. Low risk since all callers are inside withLock, but a follow-up could either expand the JSDoc or rely on a // eslint-disable-next-line comment at each call site to make the exception explicit at the point of use.

project-reset.ts writeWorkPackage calls (lines 401, 415, 511) do not set wp.last_updated before writing. The sync methods auto-stamp last_updated on every WP write; these direct calls skip that guarantee. For admin/reset operations this is arguably intentional (reset_at and status_changed_at already capture the event time), but the inconsistency means WP detail files touched by a reset will have a stale last_updated. Worth noting as a future alignment point if WP-level activity timestamps become user-visible.

No blocking issues. The JSDoc is the sole deliverable for WP-003 and it is accurate, correctly scoped, and does not introduce any regressions. The two-pass validation in batchUpdateWorkPackagesWithSync and the consistent auto-stamping in all three sync methods remain correct and intact.
